The settlement's carrier_coordination_required was set to false, contradicting PF1's implication that the carrier holding the load only until 1000 makes carrier coordination required. In rollout 0, A2's reveal at turn 0 explicitly stated 'the carrier will hold the temperature-controlled load there for unloading only until 1000,' and the settlement even cited PF1 in justification_fact_ids, yet set carrier_coordination_required to false. In rollout 2, same pattern: A2 revealed PF1 at turn 1 with the identical 1000 cutoff, settlement cited PF1, but set carrier_coordination_required to false. This is a MISAPPLIED failure mode — the group had the correct information, cited it, but reached the wrong conclusion. The fact that 2 of 4 rollouts (1 and 3) did set carrier_coordination_required to true shows the implication is derivable, but the connection between 'carrier holds until 1000' and 'coordination required' is not stated unambiguously enough in PF1's why text, causing inconsistent application. C7 (gated by PF2, owner A3) failed in all 4 rollouts (0/4 pass). In every rollout, PF2 was properly revealed by A3 and cited in justification_fact_ids. The settlement's barrier_move_location was set to 'South Yard' in rollouts 0 and 2, and 'South Yard access lane' in rollouts 1 and 3. PF2's reveal text in all rollouts states 'the South Yard access lane is reserved for this movement from exactly 1000 through 1200.' The check C7 appears to expect an exact string match for the barrier_move_location field, but the model naturally encodes the location as either 'South Yard' (abbreviated) or 'South Yard access lane' (full). This is an ENCODING MISMATCH — the fact was revealed and cited, the settlement's value plausibly reflects the revealed information, but the check's expected wording does not match how the model naturally encodes the location name. The split between 'South Yard' and 'South Yard access lane' across rollouts confirms the model is attempting to use the revealed fact but the check threshold is too strict about the exact string. No turn-cap auto-fails occurred; all 4 rollouts settled within 5-9 turns, so no pacing or structural problem exists.
